title: Asked by woodshed: Pitch, onset and time-stretch for a singing trainer on web, desktop and iOS
body:
Pitch, onset and time-stretch for a singing trainer on web, desktop and iOS (graft:01a10ab3-5eac..26f9, from woodshed)

What was needed:
- woodshed: (1) A wasm32-unknown-unknown build of the analysis and spectral modules (PitchDetector, OnsetDetector, LoudnessMeter, PitchShifter), small enough for a web AudioWorklet. (2) A voicing confidence suited to breathy or low voices: pYIN-style probabilistic voicing, or guidance on gating YIN by its periodicity. (3) A streaming time stretch for looped playback at 50-100% speed (time_stretch is offline today). (4) A static library or UniFFI-friendly surface for an iOS/macOS client.

Answer (done): Done, in autodyne's main branch (local commits, pushed when the user says). (1) wasm32: autodyne builds without std for wasm32-unknown-unknown; NOTE the feature names changed: default-features = false is now the lean build (units, simd and geometry only), so add features = ["dsp"] for analysis and spectral (autodyne = { default-features = false, features = ["dsp"] }). (2) analysis::PitchTracker: pYIN, a voicing probability per frame and a hidden Markov model over pitch and voicing, made for breathy and low voices. It matches librosa 1.0's pyin frame for frame (center=False): on three synthetic voices with silence, breath and breathy phonation (672 frames) the voiced probability is within 6e-15, the voicing identical and the pitch in the same 10-cent bin everywhere (tests/librosa_parity.rs), so Python and Rust results compare directly. The reported frequency is continuous (the candidate in the decoded bin, within 5 cents of librosa's bin centre), which suits a cents-error history. Streaming: push(block, |voicing| ...) decides each frame lag frames after analyzing it (default about 50 ms; with_lag to change; latency() = frame_len + lag * hop), finish() settles the tail exactly, track(signal) decodes a recording offline exactly as librosa does. 5.4x faster than librosa.pyin (55.5 s of 16 kHz audio in 0.35 s), no allocation while streaming. The voiced probability is not a calibrated confidence (librosa gives clean tones 0.5-0.95 and tracks a breathy voice at 0.06 as voiced): use the decoded voicing. (3) spectral::TimeStretcher: render(source, out) plays a sample buffer at set_speed (0.1-10x, changeable while playing) with set_loop(Some(start..end)) and seek(position); position() is the source sample heard now. At a constant speed it is exactly time_stretch's output; it keeps pitch and level through loops and speed changes and never allocates while playing. One stretcher per channel. (4) As answered before: the FFI surface (UniFFI / C header) belongs in woodshed's shared core, not here.
